en.title: Lost Jurassic Park Animated Series Trailer From 1993 Finally Surfaces
en.summary: A long-lost trailer for a canceled 1993 animated Jurassic Park series, titled 'Escape from Jurassic Park,' has reportedly surfaced online. This discovery has reignited fan interest in a project that never saw the light of day.
en.body:
For decades, fans have speculated about the animated adventures that might have been born from the colossal success of **Jurassic Park**. Now, a tantalizing piece of that lost history has seemingly emerged from the digital ether: a trailer for the canceled 1993 animated series, *Escape from Jurassic Park*, has reportedly surfaced online.

Uploaded by the YouTube channel **Jurassic Outpost**, the unearthed footage is believed to be a promotional reel from 1993, created by artist **William Stout** and the team at **Universal Cartoon Studios**. Stout, renowned for his paleontological artwork, was instrumental in designing the characters, creatures, and overall aesthetic for the series. The premise, as detailed by **Jurassic Park Wiki**, envisioned the return of key characters like **John Hammond**, **Alan Grant**, **Ellie Sattler**, and **Ian Malcolm** to Isla Nublar. Their mission: to recapture the escaped dinosaurs and transform the island into a dedicated research facility. Adding a familiar dynamic, **Tim** and **Lex Murphy**, the resourceful siblings from the original film, would have joined the expedition, having apparently stowed away.

## A Glimpse of What Could Have Been

The very idea of an animated *Jurassic Park* series in the early '90s was, for many, an exciting prospect. The film had captivated the globe, and its broad appeal seemed perfectly suited for the burgeoning landscape of mainstream television animation. The chance to revisit the prehistoric wonders, now rendered in a style accessible to a younger audience while still retaining the thrill of the source material, held immense potential. This trailer's reappearance offers a rare, albeit brief, window into that unfulfilled vision, showcasing the artistic direction and narrative threads that might have defined a new chapter in the *Jurassic Park* saga.

## The Allure of Lost Media

The discovery of this trailer has understandably sent ripples through the *Jurassic Park* fandom and the wider 'lost media' community. Such finds are treasures, offering tangible connections to projects that were conceived but ultimately abandoned, often due to shifting studio priorities, creative differences, or simply the sheer difficulty of bringing ambitious visions to fruition. The excitement surrounding *Escape from Jurassic Park*'s trailer is a testament to the enduring power of the franchise and the deep engagement fans have with its lore. It sparks conversation about creative paths not taken and fuels speculation about how the series might have evolved the *Jurassic Park* universe.

## What's Next

While the trailer itself is a significant discovery, details regarding the full scope of the *Escape from Jurassic Park* project or potential future unearthed materials have not yet been announced. Fans will likely continue to scour archives and online communities for any further remnants of this lost animated series.

content_raw: News Jurassic Park Long-Lost Trailer for Canceled Jurassic Park Animated Series Reportedly Surfaces Online The reportedly unearthed trailer shows what could have been By Matthew Byrd | Published on November 2, 2026 Photo Credit: Universal Pictures Comment 0 Share New Share Jurassic Park Animated Series Reportedly Surfaces Online&url= target=”_blank” title=”Twitter”> Jurassic Park Animated Series Reportedly Surfaces Online” target=”_blank” title=”Pinterest”> Photo Credit: Universal Pictures A long-sought trailer for a never-produced Jurassic Park animated series known as Escape from Jurassic Park has made its way online and reignited some discussion about one of the most famous ’90s cartoons that never was. The trailer embedded below was uploaded by the YouTube channel Jurassic Outpost, which identifies it as a promotional reel produced by William Stout and the team at Universal Cartoon Studios in 1993. The outlet was also kind enough to share some details about the story behind the footage, which they’ve previously covered on their website. Around 1993, artist William Stout (whose work spans decades and many mediums, though he is especially well known for his paleontological art) worked with Universal Cartoon Studios to design the characters, creatures, and world for an animated series based on Jurassic Park . As you’re probably thinking to yourself, an animated series based on the movie sounds pretty great. Jurassic Park was just about the biggest thing in the world at that time, and it had that kind of “for everyone” appeal that fit into the rapidly maturing world of mainstream television animation that was so popular at the time. Plus, dinosaurs. A previously shared copy of the show’s proposed season one story arc reveals just how ambitious the show was. Though it would have starred the major surviving characters from the film, the show’s plot would have featured elements similar to those later seen in The Lost World novel, including a genetics company called BioSyn that steals dinosaur eggs in the hopes of starting its own resort (where nothing can possibly go wrong). The series was reportedly intended for a slightly more mature (though still family-friendly) primetime audience, and the show’s outline certainly conveys the idea that it wasn’t going to shy away from more complex stories. So what happened to the series? Not all of the details are known, but the story goes that Stout and the team at Universal Cartoon Studios produced a trailer for the show that was intended to be shown to Steven Spielberg for approval. According to Stout, Spielberg never even watched the trailer. As Stout recounted during a 2021 convention appearance , Spielberg had grown tired of the extensive Jurassic Park merchandising and marketing and reportedly declined to pursue the project.
